text:
Martin Necas took a scary hit against Utah on Nov. 18, then came back the next night against Anaheim with two assists. That turned out to be timely. The Hockey Writers framed the week bluntly: "Avalanche's Necas Will Be Put to the Test With MacKinnon Sidelined." Colorado's offense now leans on a winger who has 26 points in 23 games and one of the hardest shots in the league (his top recorded shot is in the 96th percentile).

The goals have outrun the chances a bit: 10 goals on 6.4 expected (expected goals measure chance quality), a 20% shooting rate after 18% last season. Evolving-Hockey made him the 11th most valuable forward in the league last season, worth 3.4 wins, while noting his teammates ranked in the 99th percentile, which is the question now. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him as a high-end setup man, 10.4 primary shot assists per 60. Over his last ten games his line has created more than our numbers expected, so the playmaking looks sturdy. What we'd watch is whether that holds without MacKinnon drawing the other team's best.
headline: With MacKinnon out, Necas becomes the engine
